the-kiltartan-poetry-book-prose-translat: Lady Gregory — the great patron of the Irish literary revival — renders Irish folk poetry into beautiful English prose. Songs and verses gathered around Kiltartan, in her native Galway, speak of love, exile, and the old gods. The collection helped the world hear Ireland's native voice, and it still sings.
children-of-the-bush: Henry Lawson, Australia's beloved storyteller, gathers tales of the bush — swagmen, selectors, drovers, and the hard, free life of the outback. His dry humor and deep sympathy for battlers made him a national treasure. The classic short stories of Australia, told by a master.
beside-the-bonnie-brier-bush: Ian Maclaren's beloved stories of Drumtochty — the Scottish parish of the bonnie brier bush — charmed the world with their pathos and humor. Dominie, doctor, and villagers live in these tender pages. The book that made Scotland weep and smile. Lachlan Campbell, Drumsheugh, and Weelum MacLure remain among fiction's immortals.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-act-of-settle: A 1913 entry on the Irish Act of Settlement of 1662 — the law that sealed the Cromwellian land grab. Arthur Ua Clerigh tells its bitter story. Catholic owners lost three counties in four. Ireland's wound, set in statute.
